needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Installer verification fixtures (AC1-AC4)
        run: bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh

  # SEC-07 follow-up (#1015 incident): the release install.sh pins by default
  # must itself carry signed provenance — otherwise a fresh curl|sh refuses
  # the installer's own default with E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING. Runs the pin
  # gate live (network to github.com releases, read-only) on EVERY PR — no
  # path gating, same reasoning as installer-verify. Fixture coverage of the
  # gate's failure modes lives in installer-verify (contract 5).
  install-pin-gate:
    name: Install pin provenance gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Pinned release must carry signed provenance
        run: bash scripts/check_install_pin.sh

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, model-switch-reg, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-goldens, flutter-app-lock-smoke, office-addin-suite, extension-size-gate]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "goldens     = ${{ needs.flutter-app-goldens.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
          echo "office-addin  = ${{ needs.office-addin-suite.result }}"
          echo "ext-size-gate = ${{ needs.extension-size-gate.result }}"
          echo "model-switch-reg = ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the quality gate is NOT re-run by
  # the release twin — the release-dedupe pre-check (gh-1625) short-circuits
  # every gate leg when the tag's GREEN push run already gates it, while
  # the release-specific legs (binaries attach, release-provenance,
  # installer-smoke) keep running on the twin (the retired comment here
  # only made the binaries UPLOAD idempotent — duplicate create +
  # --clobber, last wins — while the full 35-40 min gate still re-ran,
  # doubling release wall time).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)

pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fa --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/gh995_artifact_action_pins_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          # gh-2200: rerun --failed never fires the gh-1412 retry (the
          # first attempt's upload succeeded), so without this the rerun
          # uploads a SECOND same-named artifact and download-artifact
          # pattern-mode resolves the STALE previous-attempt report — the
          # pty-coverage-gate then merges a truncated shard json and
          # phantom-fails "budgeted suite did not run" (run 43752856871
          # attempt 2). The latest attempt's evidence must win.
          overwrite: true
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()

    fix(2262): lease sidecar writes atomic (tmp+rename) on every writer (#2279)
    
    * fix(2262): lease sidecar writes atomic (tmp+rename) on every writer
    
    - heartbeat rewrites the sidecar through tmp+rename, same as acquire:
      the ~4s beat was the largest torn-read exposure window, and a torn
      read fail-opens inspect to 'free' -> a second owner drives the same
      session JSONL.
    - non-renamable backends (E5, pure web) keep a documented fallback:
      single write + post-write verify (acquire never publishes a sidecar
      there, so no reader-facing tear in normal flow).
    - inspect retries an undecodable sidecar briefly before the documented
      E4 fail-open: a torn read heals in milliseconds, a genuinely corrupt
      file stays fail-open after the bound.
    - acquire sweeps orphan publish tmps of dead publishers (crash between
      tmp write and rename); fresh in-flight tmps survive via the
      staleAfter age check.
    
    * chore: re-trigger validation (runner disconnect)

119:#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
1312:    # without stretching the watchdog much.
1327:      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
4019:  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
4026:  watchdog:
4032:    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
4034:    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
4079:          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
4081:            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:

The minimal fix addressing the ROOT of the ticket ("[ci-red] v1.0.745 failed — Quality gate red on the tag"):

**Fix: give the tag/release path the same degraded-runner self-heal the PR path already has, and teach the trip detector the job-level-timeout kill mode.**

Concretely in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
1. Watchdog `if:` — extend from `pull_request`-only to also run on tag pushes: `github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`. The retrigger mechanism differs though: for a PR it pushes an empty commit to the PR branch (which re-fires CI via... wait, pushes fire NO CI on branches! "Dispatch-only CI on PR heads: pushes fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger." Hmm — so how does the empty-commit push retrigger CI for a PR? The push doesn't fire CI directly... it fires the SM? Machine SM watches branches? Actually the SM dispatches CI when "validate-fresh / validate-armed rules" — the empty commit invalidates validation freshness → SM re-dispatches CI. Clever chain.

For a TAG push: pushing an empty commit to... a tag? You can't push an empty commit to an existing tag without moving the tag (bad — the tag is the release identity; moving v* tags would re-trigger auto_release/dedup machinery). The remedy for a degraded tag run must be a RERUN or a re-dispatch.

The workflow comment says "NEVER gh run rerun: it reallocates into the same degraded pool" — hmm, that claim ("same pool") is about the PR context (rerun reuses the same... actually gh run rerun re-allocates fresh runners too, but the comment asserts the pool is degraded as a whole). Their established remedy is a NEW run (fresh allocation) — for tags, the natural new-run trigger is `workflow_dispatch` of the CI workflow on the tag ref? `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref v1.0.745`? workflow_dispatch on a tag ref works (dispatch to a tag ref is allowed? The CI workflow has workflow_dispatch input releaseDispatch etc. — a bare validation dispatch "stays inert" (releaseDispatch=false default). And the concurrency group `ci-<ref>` — for the tag ref, a second run would queue/cancel... `cancel-in-progress` only for pull_request, so the dispatched run would QUEUE behind... no wait, the first run is COMPLETED (dead), so no queue. The dispatch would run the full gate fresh on the same tag SHA.

Hold on — but is adding a tag-path retrigger with dispatch the right MINIMAL fix, or should I fix the ACTUAL hang instead? Let me reconsider the priority:

The ticket is the CI red itself. Root cause of the RED:
- Proximate: package:test coverage race → 40-min hang → timeout kill → cancelled shard → aggregate red.
- The race is upstream (dart-lang/test) but AMPLIFIED in-repo by: (a) `--coverage` on a 25-file PTY shard on the shared arm pool; (b) no bound on the wedged state (job eats 40 min); (c) no self-heal on the release path; (d) watchdog can't even see `cancelled` jobs.

What can a minimal in-repo fix do about the race itself? Hmm — the hang is INSIDE dart test's own machinery (waiting for the isolate). Per-test timeouts can't fire (no test running). The `--timeout` flag doesn't bound suite teardown. There's `timeout-minutes: 40` on the job (already there). So the wedge is unbounded-except-by-job-timeout. 

Options for the wedge:
1. Wrap `dart test` in a bash-level watchdog: run dart test in background, poll its progress (e.g., the file-reporter json or a heartbeat), kill + fail loudly if no progress for N minutes. That's added complexity in the workflow step — a bigger change.
2. A dart_test.yaml-level fix? No — package:test can't bound it.
3. **Retry the shard**: GitHub job-level `retry` isn't native. The watchdog empty-commit retrigger is the repo's canonical retry mechanism.

Given the repo's OWN doctrine (issue #194 point 4): "A timeout means this run landed on a degraded runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh allocation; NEVER gh run rerun... One retrigger max per head commit" — the repo's canonical answer for THIS failure mode is the watchdog retrigger. The bug: the release path (tags — the ONLY push events left in this workflow!) doesn't have it. That's a genuine gap in the workflow's design: gh-1537 retired main-push CI, making tag runs the only push CI, and the watchdog never covered them.

And the trip detector gap: it scans `conclusion=="failure"` jobs only — GitHub's job-level timeout produced conclusion `cancelled` here (observed twice). The watchdog is blind to the exact kill mode it was built for. THAT is also a genuine bug in the watchdog.

So the minimal targeted fix: **extend the watchdog to the release path + make trip detection see timeout-killed jobs regardless of job conclusion**. 

Implementation sketch in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
- Watchdog `if:` → `always() && (pull_request same-repo) || (push && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v'))`.

And `runs-on` checkout of the ref works. And the `changes` classifier under dispatch uses merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) — for a tag it may behave oddly (path gating)! Hmm — for a tag dispatch, `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` with releaseDispatch=false → "bare validation dispatches stay inert" (no release). Would the gate legs run? The `changes` classifier on a dispatch derives "the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)" — for a TAG ref, origin/main vs the tag commit: if the tag == main head, diff empty → classifier says... "no changes → skip most legs"?? That would make the dispatched run green trivialy — DANGEROUS for a release gate!

Hmm. Wait — how does the RELEASE twin work then? The `release: published` event runs the same workflow with release-dedupe: "the tag's GREEN push run already gates it" — dedupe short-circuits gates because the PUSH run on the tag was green. So the tag PUSH run is the gate of record.

If the push run was RED, dedupe=false → the release twin (release: published event) runs the FULL gate itself!

The auto-release flow: "Every push to main cuts annotated tag (scripts/auto_release.sh); the tag is the single version source; releases go DRAFT-first and publish at release-provenance". Hmm — "Publish to pub.dev: success" was in the tag run's check-runs — the publish job consumes dart_ok — dart_ok must have been TRUE?! Interesting: "Publish to pub.dev: success" while quality-gate failed — per #1368, publish is gated on dart_ok only, and our red was PLATFORM-class (pty-integration-linux = cancelled → platform_red, dart_blocker empty → dart_ok=true!). EXACTLY the #1368 design: a red platform leg reddens the required aggregate but dart_ok stays true, so the pure-Dart publish proceeded. The release then... "Create Mobile GitHub Release: success", "Submit iOS to TestFlight: success", "Submit Android to Play: success", "Attach to release: success", "Installer smoke: skipped"... and "Advance vpinned marker: FAILURE" + "Summary + self-filed issues: FAILURE".

So the tag's release COMPLETED (mobile releases, TestFlight, Play, pub.dev) despite the red aggregate?! And the vpinned marker + summary jobs failed. Hmm — so what did the red actually block? Per the comment: "the aggregate itself stays the single required check" — for TAG runs there's no branch protection... The "Summary + self-filed issues" job failed though. Let me quickly check what THAT job does — its failure might be the ACTUAL gate the release cares about... It ran at 05:57:46 — BEFORE quality-gate (06:13)! Weird. It's probably the schedule/summary job of a DIFFERENT workflow on the same SHA. Whatever.

Let me refocus. WHAT SHOULD THE FIX BE for THIS TICKET, minimal and root-cause-true?

The red = Quality gate aggregate failed because pty-integration-linux was killed by its 40-min timeout (cancelled) under pool load — a degraded-runner flake of the kind the repo ALREADY classifies as "not a product defect" (see gh-2231's closed comment: "same load-dependent flake family... not a product defect") — but the release path lacks the watchdog self-heal, and the watchdog can't detect this kill mode anyway.

Minimal fix options:
A. **Watchdog: cover tag pushes + detect timeout-killed jobs by 'cancelled' job conclusion.** Release path self-heals. But: tag retrigger mechanics (dispatch on tag → classifier gating) need care.

B. **Give the hung dart test a bounded death**: make the shard step detect the wedge (e.g., wrap with `timeout` + progress heartbeat) and fail FAST (in ~minutes, not 40). Then GitHub concludes failure (not cancelled)... and quality-gate still red. Doesn't self-heal either.

C. **Address the coverage race directly**: upgrade package:test/coverage pins to a version where the disposed-connection race doesn't wedge the runner. Check current pins first. If upstream fixed `_waitForExitCode` hang handling, the pin bump is THE minimal root fix.

2. The suite VM's `_waitForExitCode` isolate is blocked in waitpid because the test's `fa` child LIVES (kill() didn't land / child ignored SIGTERM and escalation didn't happen for this instance).
3. Suite VM cannot exit (VM exit handshake waits for ALL isolates to check in — the blocking waitpid isolate never yields) → never reports exit code → runner waits forever → job runs out its 40 minutes.
4. Quality gate red via cancelled needs → ci-red ticket.

Hmm, but which is it — did the child survive, or is this purely the coverage race with a normally-exiting VM? If the VM were exiting normally, the exit-code wait would END (process exits, runner gets code). The runner waited 39 minutes = the suite VM process NEVER EXITED = the suite VM was WEDGED = a live child or a stuck isolate. The suite VM process must have been alive-but-wedged the whole 39 min. So the PRIMARY event: **the suite VM could not exit** — because of the pty2 blocking-waitpid isolate + a surviving fa child. The coverage "Service connection disposed" is then a SECONDARY symptom: the VM service died when the VM began its (wedged) shutdown handshake.

Wait — actually even simpler: maybe NO coverage race at all. Think: suite tests all pass → test_core closes suite → collects coverage → VM service connection "disposed" — why? Because the suite VM STARTED EXITING (teardown complete → VM exit handshake starts) WHILE coverage was still being gathered (under load, the gather is slow; the VM service channel closes as the VM shuts down). The VM then wedges in the exit handshake on the blocking waitpid isolate (surviving child) → never exits → runner's coverage RPC already errored ("Service connection disposed") → runner unhandled error → runner waits exit code forever. Under NORMAL load, coverage finishes BEFORE the VM begins shutdown → no error → VM wedges ONLY IF a child survived... but on green runs the VM exits fine — meaning normally the child is properly reaped (kill + escalation works), and the VM exit handshake completes.

So there are TWO co-factors:
(A) The load-timing race (coverage gather vs VM service teardown) — produces the coverage error but by itself is benign-ish (dart-lang/test would proceed...).
(B) The suite VM hanging in its exit handshake — the blocking waitpid isolate stuck on a surviving child — turns any disruption into an infinite wedge.

Hmm — but honestly, (B) alone explains everything: at suite close the VM begins exiting; waitpid isolate can't die (child alive) → VM wedges in handshake → VM service socket closes mid-handshake → coverage gather (running at that instant) errors with disposed → runner unhandled error + waits exit code forever. On green runs the child is reaped before teardown → VM exits cleanly → coverage done before teardown → all fine. Under load everything is slower, widening the window... but a surviving child isn't load-dependent unless the kill mechanism itself is racy under load.

Hmm wait — is there really a surviving child on the hang runs? If the child survived and the VM wedged, then on the 40-min killed job, the "Cleaning up orphan processes" at job teardown showed: "Terminate orphan process: pid (2537) (dart:concatenat)" and "pid (2602) (dart:dartdev_ao)" — dart processes, no `fa` AOT child listed! Only two dart orphan processes (the concatenation/AOT dev compiler helpers). No surviving fa! Hmm — that weakens (B). Although... the runner kills the process tree by group; maybe fa was in the same group and got killed at job teardown before listing. The listing shows what survived IN THE RUNER'S accounting.

Ugh. OK. Let me look at resume_tail_grid_pty_test.dart to see exactly what it spawns and how it tears down. And the harness kill path with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE. Let me also check gh-2208's test/fix to understand the escalation contract.

172:  release-pending:
260:  release-dedupe:
294:  changes:
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627, on a plain workflow_dispatch arm). The
      # check step itself is UNCONDITIONAL (no job-level if — a skipped
      # pre-check would empty its output), so the checkout must be too:
      # every arm that runs the step needs the file present. A shallow +
      # blobless fetch costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget — the
      # price of keeping the decision extracted to a script that the
      # static gate fixture-self-tests (the alternative, inlining like
      # release-pending, would orphan the selftested script; release-
      # pending stays checkout-free only because its logic IS inline).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set — live on
      # pull_request events AND on SM validation dispatches: the paths
      # step derives the validated diff from merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)
      # when no pull_request context exists (fail-safe — a classification
      # failure runs the leg, never skips it).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # Issue #1267 N2: the diff modified flutter_app/pubspec.lock — the
      # transitive-drift vector that kept linux/windows release builds red
      # for five nights (#1265). Same path-triggered model as exzone.
      locksmoke: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.locksmoke }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}

#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release

# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).

# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;

release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
          fi
          echo "release pending: $pending"
          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1625: dedupe the release-event twin of a tag run. The v* tag push
  # fires the full quality gate by design (the release pipeline keys on
  # the tag and the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes — gh-1537/gh-1172);
  # the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
  # identical gate (observed on v1.0.580: push run 38687023638 in_progress
  # + release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
  # concurrency group below — the 35-40 min gate ran twice per release).
  # This pre-check mirrors `release-pending` above: it runs on EVERY event
  # (no job-level if — a skipped pre-check would empty its output and the
  # implicit-success() default would force-skip every leg that needs it)
  # and short-circuits in the script (scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh,
  # fixture-self-tested in Static gates):
  #   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the push event
  #   with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only a
  #   GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
  #   group the push twin is already completed when this check executes,
  #   so a failed/cancelled push run degrades to the full-gate safety net
  #   below and the twin goes red on the same commit, attaching nothing)
  #   within the last 6h → dedupe=true: every gate leg ANDs
  #   `needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'` into its `if` and
  #   skips. The twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
  #   binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
  #   release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
  #   stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it — the push
  #   twin already attached/published.
  #   no recent push run (release cut on an OLD tag, or a tag the release
  #   created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) → dedupe=false:
  #   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net
  #   (AC2).
  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1625
# release-dedupe pre-check (scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh, the
# release-dedupe job in ci.yml).
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate; the `release: published`
# event for the same tag used to fire a second identical gate. The check
# must dedupe exactly the fresh-GREEN-twin case and fail safe everywhere
# else. Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no token):
#   AC1  a recent push run for the tag with conclusion == "success"
#        dedupes: the release twin skips every gate leg, the
#        release-specific legs (binaries attach, release-provenance
#        signing, installer smoke) keep running;
#   FC   FAIL-CLOSED (gh-1625 review): a failed/cancelled/in-progress
#        push run does NOT dedupe — the release twin re-runs the full
#        gate, goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing. Behind
#        the shared ci-<ref> concurrency group (cancel-in-progress:
#        false, tag runs never cancelled) the push twin is already
#        completed when the release twin's check executes, so
#        success-only is strictly safe: any other outcome degrades to
#        the AC2 full-gate safety net, never to a skipped gate;
#   AC2  no recent push run (an old tag's release, or a tag the release
#        created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) does NOT
#        dedupe: the full gate stays the safety net;
#   AC3  non-release arms (push/schedule/workflow_dispatch) short-circuit
#        with NO API call at all;
#   AC5  a failing `gh run list` degrades to dedupe=false with a loud
#        ::warning:: and a zero exit — the gate decides, never the pre-check;
#   RG   the output contract: the output file carries EXACTLY the
#        `dedupe=<bool>` line (annotations go to stdout, never into
#        GITHUB_OUTPUT), and the lookup shape is --workflow ci.yml
#        --branch <tag> --event push, --json createdAt,conclusion,status
#        with the fail-closed select(.conclusion == "success") projection.
# Same discipline as sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh (gh-1568, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/release_dedupe_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"

arguments.content:
# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The v1.0.745 release-gate CI run ([run 4424840840](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/4424840840)) went red — the aggregate `Quality gate` job failed and the ci-red-report leg auto-filed gh-2290 — while the identical tree passes the same gate green when the shared arm pool is quiet.

**Root cause** (three layers, exact locations):

1. **The kill (proximate)**: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` started 05:32:50Z and was killed at 06:13:10Z — exactly its `timeout-minutes: 40` budget (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `pty-integration-linux`) — with job conclusion **`cancelled`** (verified via the jobs API on both surviving hung jobs, 134588877581 and 134566192421). The shard log shows the suite VM for `test/integration/resume_tail_grid_pty_test.dart` entering its exit handshake right after its last test passed, then wedging forever: `getSourceReport: (-32000) Service connection disposed` during the per-suite coverage gather (`package:test_core/src/runner/vm/platform.dart:743 _gatherCoverage`), followed by `Attempt:11..2350 waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in` every second until the job kill. `_waitForExitCode` is the vendored pty2 fork's blocking-`waitpid` helper isolate (`vendor/pty2/lib/src/pty.dart:130`); `vendor/pty2/lib/src/pty_core.dart:19` documents exactly this wedge class ("pty2's blocking `waitpid` isolate cannot die while the child lives, and it wedges the Dart VM's exit handshake" — the gh-2208/#2122 family, CI runs 43835937617/43151400571). `dart test` therefore never completes, the job burns its whole 40-minute budget, `pty-integration-linux` needs-result = `cancelled`, and the `quality-gate` aggregate fails on `platform_red` (ci.yml `quality-gate` step "Fail on any real failure").
2. **The trigger (load, not code)**: this is a load-dependent race on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, not a product regression — the exact tag tree `5a51fa42` passed full CI green 36 minutes earlier on the flake-quarantine branch (`4fe2ff09`, run 44240617362, 04:55Z) with the same shard-2 target list, and `cde9fbbc` passed again at 05:55Z (run 44247625390). The hang occurred on three runs in the 03:58–05:31Z SM-dispatch wave (751d8778, ea74d200, the tag) and never on the quieter ones. The ci.yml `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE` comment (#1391) documents this pool-contention class.
3. **The missing self-heal (the actionable defect)**: the repo's designed remedy for a timeout-type failure — the `watchdog` job ("A timeout means this run landed on a degraded runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push... One retrigger max per head commit", ci.yml `watchdog`, issue #194 point 4) — is gated `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` **only**. Since gh-1537 retired main-push CI, v* tag pushes are the ONLY push events this workflow receives, i.e. the release gate — the exact path that filed this ticket — has no watchdog (its check-run on the tag run is `skipped`). Additionally the trip detector scans `select(.conclusion=="failure")` jobs whose last step is `cancelled`, but GitHub concluded the timeout-killed job `cancelled` (not `failure`) on both hung shards, so this kill mode is invisible to the watchdog even on pull_request events.

**Impact**: every time a release-tag run hits a degraded-runner timeout, the release gate goes red, a ci-red ticket is filed, and the tag stays red until the next tag happens to go green ("Closes manually when the ref goes green") — no self-heal, and ~40 minutes of burned 40-min-budget runner time per occurrence. Product code is unaffected; pub.dev publish correctly stayed `dart_ok=true` (platform-class red, #1368).

**Fix approach**: make the release path self-heal exactly as PRs already do — (a) extract the watchdog trip decision into a fixture-testable script `scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh` that trips on the timeout-kill signature (job conclusion `failure` **or** `cancelled` with last step `cancelled`) and never on real test failures (last step failed); (b) let the watchdog run on v* tag pushes; (c) for the tag arm, retrigger via `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <tag>` (GITHUB_TOKEN may trigger workflow_dispatch — github.blog 2022-09-08; `release-pending` never blocks dispatch arms, dedupe is false for non-release events, so the dispatch re-runs the full gate on the tag's exact tree) with a one-shot guard (a previous `workflow_dispatch` run for the tag ref suppresses re-firing); (d) fixture self-test the trip script (`scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh`, release-dedupe #1100 pattern) wired into the static gate, plus a workflow-shape guard test.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-2290. Related prior art, not fixes for this: gh-2208 (shutdownPty reap-or-throw for leaked pty children — ran clean here; the harness teardowns completed), #2228 (quarantined `jsr_cli_test.dart`, unrelated to the hang), gh-2231 (v1.0.739 red, closed as the same load-dependent flake family with no workflow change).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_check.sh — the gh-2290 timeout-kill trip decision for the
# `watchdog` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml (issue #194 point 4).
#
# The watchdog's remedy for a degraded-runner allocation is ONE retrigger
# with a fresh allocation (never `gh run rerun`). Tripping requires
# recognizing the job-level timeout KILL — and only that kill:
#
#   job conclusion == "failure" OR "cancelled"   (GitHub lands a
#     `timeout-minutes` kill on either shape: the classic form is
#     failure-with-cancelled-last-step, but the v1.0.745 tag run's hung
#     PTY shard — jobs 134588877581/134566192421, run 4424840840 — was
#     concluded `cancelled` outright)
#   AND the job's LAST step conclusion == "cancelled"  (the kill cuts a
#     step mid-flight; a real test failure ENDS with a failed step, so a
#     genuine red never retrigs — a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a
#     product/test defect)
#
# A cancelled job with NO steps (never started — a run-level cancel
# reaching a queued job) is NOT a timeout kill. Neither is success/skipped.
#
# Network-free by contract: the caller fetches the run's jobs JSON (the
# jobs API embeds each job's steps array — one call, no per-job follow-ups)
# and hands the FILE here. Fixture-self-tested by
# scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh (#1100 pattern), wired into the static
# gate; the workflow wiring is pinned by
# test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart.
#
# Usage: watchdog_trip_check.sh [jobs-json-file] [output-file]
#   jobs-json-file  the `gh api .../runs/<id>/jobs` document; `-` or an
#                   empty arg reads stdin
#   output-file     default $GITHUB_OUTPUT when set (the trip=<bool> line
#                   lands there AND on stdout); without one, stdout only.
#                   Diagnostics never start with `trip=`, so the line is
#                   unambiguous in both sinks.
set -u

json_file="${1:--}"
out_file="${2:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}}"

if [ "$json_file" = "-" ] || [ -z "$json_file" ]; then
  jobs_json="$(cat)"
else
  jobs_json="$(cat "$json_file")"
fi

# The timeout-kill signature, as one jq projection:
#   failed-or-cancelled jobs whose last step was cancelled.
matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '
  [.jobs[]?
   | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
   | select((.steps // []) | length > 0)
   | select(.steps[-1].conclusion == "cancelled")]
  | length')"

if [ -z "$matches" ] || ! [ "$matches" -eq "$matches" ] 2>/dev/null; then
  # A malformed projection must NEVER flip the trip (fail-safe: the
  # watchdog is an optimization — a broken pre-check degrades to no
  # retrigger, never to a spurious dispatch loop).
  echo "::warning::watchdog_trip_check: unparseable jobs JSON or jq failure — not tripping"
  matches=0
fi

trip=false
if [ "$matches" -gt 0 ]; then
  trip=true
fi

if [ "$trip" = "true" ]; then
  echo "::notice::watchdog_trip_check: $matches job(s) match the timeout-kill signature (gh-2290):"
  printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '
    (.jobs[]?
     | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
     | select((.steps // []) | length > 0)
     | select(.steps[-1].conclusion == "cancelled"))
    | "  " + .name + ": " + .conclusion + " (last step: " + .steps[-1].conclusion + ")"'
else
  echo "watchdog_trip_check: no timeout-kill signature — nothing to retrigger"
fi

if [ -n "$out_file" ]; then
  {
    printf 'trip=%s\n' "$trip"
  } >> "$out_file"
fi
echo "trip=$trip"

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-2290 watchdog
# trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh, the `watchdog` job in
# ci.yml).
#
# The v1.0.745 tag run (4424840840) hung a PTY shard on the pty2
# blocking-waitpid wedge (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode
# to check in`), burned its whole 40-minute budget, was concluded
# `cancelled` — and NOTHING retrigged: the watchdog was pull_request-only
# AND its detector scanned failure-conclusion jobs only. The decision must
# trip exactly on the timeout-kill signature and never on a genuine red.
# Proves, on fixture JSON (no network, no gh, no token):
#   AC1  the gh-2290 kill mode: job conclusion `cancelled` + last step
#        `cancelled` → trip (both hung shard jobs, 134588877581 and
#        134566192421, landed exactly here),
#   AC2  the classic kill mode: job `failure` + last step `cancelled`
#        (the original detector's shape) → trip,
#   FC1  a REAL test failure — last step `failure` — never trips: a fresh
#        runner allocation cannot fix a product/test defect,
#   FC2  success / skipped / a cancelled never-started job (no steps) /
#        an empty jobs array never trip,
#   FC3  a malformed body fails SAFE to trip=false with a warning (a
#        broken pre-check must degrade to no retrigger, never to a
#        spurious dispatch loop),
#   RG   the output contract: exactly ONE `trip=<bool>` line into the
#        output file, none of the diagnostics starting with `trip=`, and
#        multiple matches still produce a single line.
# Same discipline as release_dedupe_selftest.sh (gh-1625, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/watchdog_trip_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# fixture <name> <json> — write a fixture, run the check, return stdout.
fixture() {
  _fx_name="$1"; shift
  printf '%s' "$1" > "$TMP/$_fx_name.json"
  bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/$_fx_name.json" 2>&1
}

trip_line() { # trip_line <output> — the trip= line, empty when absent
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -E '^trip=(true|false)$' | head -1
}

trip_count() { # trip_count <output> — number of trip= lines
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$'
}

json_for() { # json_for <conclusion> <last-step-conclusion|NONE>
  cat <<EOF
{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)", "conclusion": "$1", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "$2"}]}]}
EOF
}

echo "watchdog_trip_selftest (gh-2290):"

# AC1 — the gh-2290 kill mode.
out="$(fixture ac1 "$(json_for cancelled cancelled)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC1 cancelled job + cancelled last step trips (gh-2290 kill mode)" $?

# AC2 — the classic kill mode.
out="$(fixture ac2 "$(json_for failure cancelled)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC2 failure job + cancelled last step trips (classic timeout shape)" $?

# FC1 — a real test failure must NOT retrigger.
out="$(fixture fc1 "$(json_for failure failure)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1 real test failure (last step failure) does NOT trip" $?

# FC2 — clean, skipped, never-started, empty.
out="$(fixture fc2a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Static gates", "conclusion": "success", "steps": [{"name": "analyze", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2a success job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Golden suite (macOS baselines)", "conclusion": "skipped", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2b skipped job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2c '{"jobs": [{"name": "Binaries smoke gate", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2c cancelled never-started job (no steps) does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2d '{"jobs": []}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2d empty jobs array does not trip" $?

# FC3 — malformed body fails safe.
out="$(fixture fc3 'not json at all')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC3 malformed jobs JSON fails safe to trip=false" $?
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '::warning::'
check "FC3 malformed body warns loudly" $?

# RG — output contract: exactly one trip= line; diagnostics clean.
out="$(fixture rg1 "$(json_for cancelled cancelled)")"
[ "$(trip_count "$out")" = "1" ]
check "RG1 exactly one trip= line on stdout" $?

printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -vE '^trip=' | grep -qE '^trip='
[ $? -ne 0 ]
check "RG2 no diagnostic line masquerades as trip=" $?

out_file="$TMP/github_output"
: > "$out_file"
GITHUB_OUTPUT="$out_file" bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/ac1.json" > "$TMP/rg3.out"
grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$' "$out_file" > "$TMP/rg3.count"
[ "$(cat "$TMP/rg3.count")" = "1" ]
check "RG3 exactly one trip= line lands in GITHUB_OUTPUT" $?

out="$(fixture rg4 '{"jobs": [{"name": "a", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": [{"name": "s", "conclusion": "cancelled"}]}, {"name": "b", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "s", "conclusion": "cancelled"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
[ "$(trip_count "$out")" = "1" ]
check "RG4 multiple matches trip once, one line" $?

# RG5 — stdin arm (`-`).
out="$(printf '%s' "$(json_for cancelled cancelled)" | bash "$CHECK" - 2>&1)"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "RG5 stdin arm trips" $?

if [ "$fails" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "watchdog_trip_selftest: $fails FAILURE(S)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "watchdog_trip_selftest: all green"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_check.sh — the gh-2290 timeout-kill trip decision for the
# `watchdog` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml (issue #194 point 4).
#
# The watchdog's remedy for a degraded-runner allocation is ONE retrigger
# with a fresh allocation (never `gh run rerun`). Tripping requires
# recognizing a job-level timeout KILL — and only that kill. The v1.0.745
# tag run 4424840840 hung a PTY shard (the pty2 blocking-waitpid wedge,
# `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`), burned
# its 40-minute budget and was killed by `timeout-minutes`: GitHub landed
# that kill as job conclusion `cancelled` (NOT `failure` — jobs
# 134588877581/134566192421) with the mid-flight step `cancelled` and the
# trailing `if: always()` evidence steps `skipped`.
#
# The timeout-kill signature, as one predicate over the jobs JSON:
#
#   job conclusion == "failure" OR "cancelled"      (both kill shapes land)
#   AND at least one step concluded "cancelled"      (a step was cut
#     mid-flight — the kill itself)
#   AND NO step concluded "failure"                  (a real test failure
#     ENDS with a failed step — in these shards the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps often trail it with `success` — so a genuine red
#     never trips; a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a defect)
#
# A cancelled job with NO steps (never started — a run-level cancel
# reaching a queued job) is NOT a kill. Success/skipped never trip.
#
# Network-free by contract: the caller fetches the run's jobs document in
# ONE call (the jobs API embeds each job's steps array — `gh run view
# --json jobs`; `gh api .../runs/<id>/jobs` is fine unpaged, but
# `--paginate` concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first
# page — verified against a 69-job run) and hands the FILE here.
# Fixture-self-tested by scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh (#1100
# pattern), wired into the static gate; the workflow wiring is pinned by
# test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart.
#
# Usage: watchdog_trip_check.sh [jobs-json-file] [output-file]
#   jobs-json-file  the jobs document; `-` or an empty arg reads stdin
#   output-file     default $GITHUB_OUTPUT when set (the trip=<bool> line
#                   lands there AND on stdout); without one, stdout only.
#                   Diagnostics never start with `trip=`, so the line is
#                   unambiguous in both sinks.
set -u

json_file="${1:--}"
out_file="${2:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}}"

if [ "$json_file" = "-" ] || [ -z "$json_file" ]; then
  jobs_json="$(cat)"
else
  jobs_json="$(cat "$json_file")"
fi

# The timeout-kill signature, as one jq projection:
#   failed-or-cancelled jobs with >=1 cancelled step and NO failed step.
projection='
  [.jobs[]?
   | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
   | select([.steps[]?.conclusion] | inside(["cancelled"]))
   | select(([.steps[]?.conclusion] | inside(["failure"])) | not)]
  | length'

matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "$projection")"

if [ -z "$matches" ] || ! [ "$matches" -eq "$matches" ] 2>/dev/null; then
  # A malformed projection must NEVER flip the trip (fail-safe: the
  # watchdog is an optimization — a broken pre-check degrades to no
  # retrigger, never to a spurious dispatch loop).
  echo "::warning::watchdog_trip_check: unparseable jobs JSON or jq failure — not tripping"
  matches=0
fi

trip=false
if [ "$matches" -gt 0 ]; then
  trip=true
fi

if [ "$trip" = "true" ]; then
  echo "::notice::watchdog_trip_check: $matches job(s) match the timeout-kill signature (gh-2290):"
  printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "$projection | .[]" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || true
  printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '
    [.jobs[]?
     | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
     | select([.steps[]?.conclusion] | inside(["cancelled"]))
     | select(([.steps[]?.conclusion] | inside(["failure"])) | not)]
    | (.[] | "  " + .name + ": " + .conclusion
       + " (cancelled step: "
       + ([.steps[]? | select(.conclusion == "cancelled") | .name] | join(", "))
       + ")")'
else
  echo "watchdog_trip_check: no timeout-kill signature — nothing to retrigger"
fi

if [ -n "$out_file" ]; then
  {
    printf 'trip=%s\n' "$trip"
  } >> "$out_file"
fi
echo "trip=$trip"

p = 'scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh'
s = open(p).read()

old_json_for = s[s.index('json_for() {'):s.index('trip_line() {')]
new_json_for = '''json_for() { # json_for <conclusion> <shape: kill|failure|success>
  # kill:    the REAL gh-2290 shape - the mid-flight dart test step
  #          cancelled, the trailing if:always() evidence steps skipped.
  # failure: a real test failure - the dart test step FAILED, the
  #          evidence steps still trail with success (the last step is
  #          NOT the failed one in these shards).
  # success: a clean job.
  case "$2" in
    kill)    steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "upload artifact", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "Post cache", "conclusion": "skipped"}]' ;;
    failure) steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
    *)       steps='[{"name": "run", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
  esac
  cat <<JEOF
{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)", "conclusion": "$1", "steps": $steps}]}
JEOF
}

'''
s = s.replace(old_json_for, new_json_for)

i1 = s.index('# AC1 ')
i2 = s.index('# FC2 ')
new_12 = '''# AC1 - the gh-2290 kill mode (the REAL shape: conclusion cancelled,
# mid-flight step cancelled, trailing always()-evidence steps skipped).
out="$(fixture ac1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC1 cancelled job with a cancelled step trips (gh-2290 kill mode)" $?

# AC2 - the classic kill mode (failure conclusion, cut step, no failed step).
out="$(fixture ac2 "$(json_for failure kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC2 failure job with a cancelled step and no failed step trips" $?

# FC1 - a real test failure must NOT retrigger (both shapes: failed step
# last, and failed step TRAILED by always()-evidence steps - the shape
# every red pty shard actually lands in).
out="$(fixture fc1a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 0/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1a real test failure (failed step, trailing evidence) does NOT trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc1b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 3/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "setup", "conclusion": "success"}, {"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1b real test failure (failed LAST step) does NOT trip" $?

'''

i4 = s.index('# RG5')

[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
'''
s = s[:i3] + new_rg4 + s[i4:]

s = s.replace('json_for cancelled cancelled)', 'json_for cancelled kill)')
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('patched ok')

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-2290 watchdog
# trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh, the `watchdog` job in
# ci.yml).
#
# The v1.0.745 tag run (4424840840) hung a PTY shard on the pty2
# blocking-waitpid wedge (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode
# to check in`), burned its whole 40-minute budget, was concluded
# `cancelled` — and NOTHING retrigged: the watchdog was pull_request-only
# AND its detector scanned failure-conclusion jobs only. The decision must
# trip exactly on the timeout-kill signature and never on a genuine red.
# Proves, on fixture JSON (no network, no gh, no token):
#   AC1  the gh-2290 kill mode: job conclusion `cancelled`, the
#     mid-flight step `cancelled`, trailing `if: always()` evidence
#     steps `skipped` — the EXACT shape of hung shard jobs
#     134588877581/134566192421 → trip,
#   AC2  the classic kill mode: job `failure`, a cut `cancelled` step,
#     no failed step → trip,
#   FC1  a REAL test failure never trips — in either landing shape: the
#     failed step LAST, or the failed step TRAILED by the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps (`success`) that every red pty shard actually
#     leaves behind (last-step-success — the old last-step detector was
#     blind to this too),
#   FC2  success / skipped / a cancelled never-started job (no steps) /
#     an empty jobs array never trip,
#   FC3  a malformed body fails SAFE to trip=false with a warning (a
#     broken pre-check must degrade to no retrigger, never to a
#     spurious dispatch loop),
#   RG   the output contract: exactly ONE `trip=<bool>` line, no
#     diagnostic masquerading as `trip=`, GITHUB_OUTPUT lands exactly
#     one line, multiple matches still produce a single line, and the
#     stdin arm (`-`) works.
# Same discipline as release_dedupe_selftest.sh (gh-1625, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/watchdog_trip_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

fixture() { # fixture <name> <json> — write a fixture, run the check
  _fx_name="$1"; shift
  printf '%s' "$1" > "$TMP/$_fx_name.json"
  bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/$_fx_name.json" 2>&1
}

trip_line() { # trip_line <output> — the trip= line, empty when absent
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -E '^trip=(true|false)$' | head -1
}

trip_count() { # trip_count <output> — number of trip= lines
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$'
}

json_for() { # json_for <conclusion> <shape: kill|failure|success>
  # kill:    the REAL gh-2290 shape — the mid-flight dart test step
  #          cancelled, the trailing if:always() evidence steps skipped.
  # failure: a real test failure — the dart test step FAILED, the
  #          evidence steps still trail with success (the last step is
  #          NOT the failed one in these shards).
  # success: a clean job.
  case "$2" in
    kill)    steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "upload artifact", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "Post cache", "conclusion": "skipped"}]' ;;
    failure) steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
    *)       steps='[{"name": "run", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
  esac
  cat <<JEOF
{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)", "conclusion": "$1", "steps": $steps}]}
JEOF
}

echo "watchdog_trip_selftest (gh-2290):"

# AC1 — the gh-2290 kill mode (the REAL shape: conclusion cancelled,
# mid-flight step cancelled, trailing always()-evidence steps skipped).
out="$(fixture ac1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC1 cancelled job with a cancelled step trips (gh-2290 kill mode)" $?

# AC2 — the classic kill mode (failure conclusion, cut step, no failed step).
out="$(fixture ac2 "$(json_for failure kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC2 failure job with a cancelled step and no failed step trips" $?

# FC1 — a real test failure must NOT retrigger (both landing shapes).
out="$(fixture fc1a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 0/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1a real test failure (failed step, trailing evidence) does NOT trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc1b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 3/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "setup", "conclusion": "success"}, {"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1b real test failure (failed LAST step) does NOT trip" $?

# FC2 — clean, skipped, never-started, empty.
out="$(fixture fc2a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Static gates", "conclusion": "success", "steps": [{"name": "analyze", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2a success job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Golden suite (macOS baselines)", "conclusion": "skipped", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2b skipped job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2c '{"jobs": [{"name": "Binaries smoke gate", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2c cancelled never-started job (no steps) does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2d '{"jobs": []}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2d empty jobs array does not trip" $?

# FC3 — malformed body fails safe.
out="$(fixture fc3 'not json at all')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC3 malformed jobs JSON fails safe to trip=false" $?
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '::warning::'
